origins.section: The Checker Applies the Format Rules That Strict Validation Applies
A Requirement States One Behaviour With SHALL or MUST; a Scenario Says When and Then
Each Scenario Becomes a Test, and Each Test Fails Before the Code Exists

recorded.prompt:q-strict: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-strict: | the text has SHALL or MUST (in the text, not only the header) | warning | warning | ... | `--strict` fails on any warning, plain validation on errors only |

recorded.outcome:q-fail-first: A test that has never failed has not shown that it tests anything.

recorded.rule: Q2 v2: a giveaway, read from the question's own text alone
recorded.prompt:q-strict: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.outcome:q-strict: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'b'
recorded.because:q-strict: b and c share 'missing SHALL or MUST'; d's 'never' is weak; no cue singles out one option
